questions.question: Arrival counts $a_1,\dots,a_n$ are logged in many consecutive periods of equal length, each holding many arrivals. Let $\tilde{\lambda}$ be the average count and $\tilde{\sigma}^2$ the average squared count minus $\tilde{\lambda}^2$. Which expression estimates the inter-arrival SCV $C_a^2$?
options: $\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}^2$
$\tilde{\lambda}/\tilde{\sigma}^2$
$\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}$
$\tilde{\sigma}/\tilde{\lambda}$

questions.question: A call centre records only the number of calls in each one-hour slot, not the call moments; calls form a stationary stream with i.i.d. inter-arrival times and many calls per slot. Besides the arrival rate, what can these slot counts estimate about the inter-arrival times?
options: Their SCV $C_a^2$, as the variance-to-mean ratio of the slot counts
Nothing beyond the mean, since variability is lost with the call moments
Their variance $\sigma^2$, which equals the variance of the slot counts
Their whole distribution, read off from the histogram of the slot counts

questions.question: Daily arrival counts of a stationary stream (many days, many arrivals per day) give the estimate $\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}=0.4$ for the inter-arrival SCV $C_a^2$. What does this value say about the arrivals?
options: Inter-arrival times vary more than exponential ones, so arrivals cluster
Inter-arrival times have a standard deviation about $40\%$ of their mean
Each daily count typically deviates about $40\%$ from the mean count
Inter-arrival times vary less than exponential ones, so arrivals are regular

questions.question: A clinic logs arrivals per 8-hour day and computes $\tilde{\lambda}$, the mean daily count, and $\tilde{\sigma}^2$, the variance of the daily counts, to estimate the inter-arrival SCV $C_a^2\approx\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}$. Must $\tilde{\lambda}$ first be converted to an hourly rate?
options: Yes: divide $\tilde{\lambda}$ by $8$ so it matches the rate $\lambda$ in $C_a^2=\lambda^2\sigma^2$
No: $\tilde{\lambda}$ is a count per day and the ratio is unit-free, so none is needed
Yes: convert $\tilde{\sigma}^2$ to squared hours so it matches the variance $\sigma^2$
No, but the ratio must then be multiplied by $8$ to give an hourly SCV

questions.question: Arrivals have i.i.d. inter-arrival times $X_1,X_2,\dots$; $A_k=X_1+\dots+X_k$ is the time of the $k$-th arrival and $A(t)$ the number of arrivals in $[0,t]$. Which event identity links the count to the arrival times, as used to transfer the normal approximation from $A_k$ to $A(t)$?

Inter-arrival times are i.i.d. with mean $2$ minutes and variance $\sigma^2=1$ minute$^2$. Let $A(t)$ be the number of arrivals in $[0,t]$. Using the large-$t$ approximation, what is the approximate variance of $A(t)$ for $t=480$ minutes?

Arrivals were counted in $n=5$ long periods of equal length, with $\sum a_i=40$ and $\sum a_i^2=330$. With $\tilde{\lambda}$ the average count and $\tilde{\sigma}^2$ the average squared count minus $\tilde{\lambda}^2$, what is the estimate $\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}$ of $C_a^2$?

Jobs arrive with i.i.d. inter-arrival times of mean $5$ minutes and standard deviation $2$ minutes. Counts are taken over consecutive periods of length $t$. As $t\to\infty$, to which value does $\operatorname{Var}(A(t))/\mathbb{E}[A(t)]$ converge?

Arrivals form a Poisson process with rate $3$ per hour and are counted in consecutive $4$-hour periods. Over many periods, which long-run values do the average count $\tilde{\lambda}$ and the count variance $\tilde{\sigma}^2$ take?
options: $\tilde{\lambda}=12$ and $\tilde{\sigma}^2=12$
$\tilde{\lambda}=12$ and $\tilde{\sigma}^2=144$
$\tilde{\lambda}=3$ and $\tilde{\sigma}^2=3$
$\tilde{\lambda}=12$ and $\tilde{\sigma}^2=1$

questions.question: Four stations log arrival counts over many long periods; each stream is stationary with i.i.d. inter-arrival times. Mean count and count variance are: P $10$ and $15$; Q $30$ and $60$; R $120$ and $180$; S $27$ and $9$. Which station has the largest estimated inter-arrival SCV $C_a^2$?
options: Station P
Station Q
Station R
Station S

questions.question: An analyst wrongly uses $\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}^2$, computed from daily counts of a stationary renewal arrival stream with many arrivals per day, as the estimate of $C_a^2$. If two-day periods are used instead, what happens to this value?
options: It stays about the same, since it estimates $C_a^2$, which does not depend on the period
It roughly doubles, since the count variance doubles while $\tilde{\lambda}$ is a daily rate
It roughly quarters, since the mean count is squared in the denominator
It roughly halves, since count variance and mean both double and the mean is squared

questions.question: Jobs arrive exactly every $1.5$ hours, so $C_a^2=0$, and arrivals are counted in consecutive periods of length $T$ hours. Hourly counts give a ratio $\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}$ well above $0$. What happens to this ratio as $T$ grows large?
options: It stays at the hourly value, since the ratio does not depend on the period length
It tends to $1$, since long-period counts are approximately normal like Poisson counts
It tends to $0$, since counts take two neighbouring values and their variance stays bounded
It grows, since the count variance increases linearly with the period length

questions.question: To estimate $C_a^2$ by $\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}$ from counts of a stationary arrival stream with i.i.d. inter-arrival times, one needs many periods ($n$ large) and long periods (length $t$ large). Which statement about these two requirements is correct?
options: Large $n$ makes $\tilde{\lambda},\tilde{\sigma}^2$ accurate; large $t$ makes their ratio near $C_a^2$
Large $n$ alone removes the bias of short periods, since averages converge
Large $t$ alone suffices, so a single long period gives a usable estimate
Both are the same, since $n$ periods of length $t$ form one period of length $nt$

questions.question: Daily counts of a stationary arrival stream with i.i.d. inter-arrival times give mean $\tilde{\lambda}=100$ and variance $\tilde{\sigma}^2=60$, and days are long enough for the large-$t$ approximations. Approximately what variance should counts per $7$-day week have?

Jobs arrive exactly every $2$ hours, at times $0.5,2.5,4.5,\dots$, so $C_a^2=0$. Arrivals are counted per hour, in $[0,1),[1,2),[2,3),\dots$. Over many hours, what is the ratio $\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}$ of the count variance to the mean count?

Daily counts give $\tilde{\lambda}=40$ and $\tilde{\sigma}^2=20$, and service times have $C_s^2=1$. Sakasegawa's formula makes $\mathbb{E}[W]$ proportional to $(C_a^2+C_s^2)/2$ for fixed load, servers and mean service time. Compared with assuming Poisson arrivals, how does using the estimated $C_a^2$ change $\mathbb{E}[W]$?
options: About $50\%$ lower
About $50\%$ higher
About $25\%$ lower
About $75\%$ lower

questions.question: Daily counts of a stationary arrival stream with i.i.d. inter-arrival times (many days, many arrivals per day) give $\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}\approx1$. Which conclusion about the arrivals is justified?
options: $C_a^2\approx1$, but arrivals need not be Poisson: other gap distributions with SCV $1$ fit too
Arrivals are Poisson, since a count variance equal to the mean occurs only for Poisson counts
Inter-arrival times have variance about $1$, since $\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}$ estimates $\sigma^2$
$C_a^2\approx1/\tilde{\lambda}$, since the ratio must still be divided by the mean daily count

questions.question: Customers arrive in pairs: pairs form a Poisson process and both members arrive at the same moment, so gaps between consecutive customers alternate between $0$ and an exponential time. Customer counts per long period have variance-to-mean ratio $2$, while the gaps have SCV $3$. Why does the count estimator miss the gap SCV?
options: The gaps have infinite variance, so the SCV of the gaps is not defined
The gaps are not i.i.d.: a zero gap is always followed by an exponential one
The periods are too short; with longer periods the ratio would approach $3$
Customer counts are Poisson, so the ratio $2$ must be a data error

questions.question: Arrivals are counted per $8$-hour day ($480$ minutes) over many days; the stream is stationary with i.i.d. inter-arrival times, and the counts give $\tilde{\lambda}=40$ and $\tilde{\sigma}^2=10$. What is the estimated standard deviation of the inter-arrival times, in minutes?
options: $3$ minutes
$0.95$ minutes
$0.75$ minutes
$6$ minutes

questions.question: A shop logs daily arrival counts. On quiet days arrivals are Poisson with mean $10$ per day, on busy days Poisson with mean $30$, and half the logged days are of each type. Pooling all days, what is the long-run ratio $\tilde{\sigma}^2/\tilde{\lambda}$?
